references.text: In Jesus' speech against the Pharisees and the scribes in [ref:Matt 23:6-7|Matthew 23:6-7], he says exactly the same thing: they love the places of honor at banquets, the front seats in the synagogues, and to be greeted with respect in the marketplaces. This is the parallel passage in Matthew.

In [ref:Mark 12:38-39|Mark 12:38-39], Jesus warns against the scribes who like to walk around in long robes, be greeted with respect in the marketplaces, have the front seats in the synagogues, and the places of honor at banquets. This is also a parallel passage dealing with the same theme.

In [ref:Luk 14:7-11|Luke 14:7-11], Jesus speaks against those who choose the places of honor at banquets and encourages humility. This expands on the criticism of the Pharisees' desire for honor and prominent positions.

In [ref:Luk 20:46|Luke 20:46], Jesus repeats his warning against the scribes who want to be greeted with respect in the marketplaces and have the front seats in the synagogues, which directly reflects the theme in Luke 11:43.

In [ref:Joh 5:44|John 5:44], Jesus asks how they can believe when they accept glory from one another and do not seek the glory that comes from the only God. This highlights the Pharisees' fundamental problem: they seek human approval rather than God's.

In [ref:Gal 1:10|Galatians 1:10], Paul asks whether he is seeking to please people, and says that if he were still trying to please people, he would not be a servant of Christ. This contrasts the Pharisees' desire for human honor with the attitude a servant of Christ should have.

In [ref:1 Joh 2:16|1 John 2:16], the pride of life is mentioned as something that is in the world and not from the Father. The Pharisees' love for places of honor and greetings in the marketplaces is an expression of exactly this pride.

In [ref:Fil 2:3|Philippians 2:3], Paul urges believers not to do anything out of selfish ambition or vain conceit, but in humility to value others above themselves – the opposite of the attitude of the Pharisees that Jesus criticizes.
In [ref:3 Joh 1:9|3 John 1:9], Diotrephes is described as loving to be first among them, which reflects the same attitude Jesus criticizes in the Pharisees – the desire to hold the foremost position.
